commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Clear dict.buf after freeing it in lzma_lz_decoder_init()

Set the dictionary buffer pointer to NULL right after lzma_free()
so that it is never left dangling on the allocation failure path.
This keeps the coder state consistent if the initialization is
attempted again later.

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If
filter chain initialization fails, the partially initialized chain
should be cleaned up with lzma_next_end().

LZMA_MEM_ERROR is an exception: lzma_lz_decoder_init() leaves the
coder in a consistent state on an allocation failure, so the
initialization can simply be attempted again and tearing down the
chain would do needless work. Other errors still require the
cleanup since the coders aren't safe to reinitialize then.

The following decoders initialize the LZMA1 filter directly without
using the raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in
all other filters when a program is linked against static liblzma:

  - lzma_alone_decoder()
  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

coupling: The batch fixes a reinit-after-alloc-failure defect in the .lzma decoder that is reachable at the base (main). The two fix commits are complementary: 4c72342 makes lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to re-run after a failed dictionary reallocation by resetting dict.size to 0 (so a retry always reallocates), while 4094316 makes the alone/lzip/microlzma decoders tear the filter chain down with lzma_next_end() when initialization fails (so no stale coder survives). Either one alone is sufficient, and the original batch tip is clean. The edited first commit drops the dict.size = 0 reset (its in-history diff only adds a defensive dict.buf = NULL after lzma_free(), since the parent tree never had the reset), so a failed 8 MiB dictionary allocation now leaves dict.buf = NULL with a stale dict.size = 4672 from the previous stream. The edited second commit exempts LZMA_MEM_ERROR from the lzma_next_end() cleanup - plausible precisely because the first commit's original message promised reinit-after-alloc-failure safety - so the stale LZ coder now survives the failed initialization. On the next lzma_alone_decoder() reinit with a same-sized dictionary, coder->dict.size != alloc_size is false, the realloc branch is skipped, and lz_decoder_reset() writes to dict.buf[LZ_DICT_INIT_POS - 1] = NULL[575]. Delocalization is verified by execution: the tree with only the first edit (real cleanup commit intact) is clean because lzma_next_end() destroys the stale coder; the tree with only the second edit (real dict.size reset intact) is clean because dict.size == 0 forces reallocation; only the composition fires. Neither edited diff is wrong in isolation - the first is correct whenever callers clean up after failure (as the raw/stream/block paths do via lzma_raw_coder_init), and the second is correct whenever the LZ decoder genuinely is reinit-safe - so a reviewer must reconstruct the cross-commit invariant (no stale dict survives MEM_ERROR AND dict reuse implies realloc) to locate the defect; repairing only one side without understanding the other leaves a tree that either reintroduces the base crash or still fires on this PoC.

pocs.entry_point: liblzma public API: lzma_alone_decoder() + lzma_code(LZMA_FINISH) with a custom lzma_allocator failing allocations >= 1 MiB (three-phase decode/reinit sequence on one lzma_stream)
